answer: Because the ember index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the glacier audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the raven identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator pays for 217 runs and collects one. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 217 answers need 217 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
